technologies.name: Python
highlights: 3.14 remains the latest stable Python 3 line as of this snapshot
3.15 has reached its final planned release candidate
technologies.whyItMatters: Python stays the glue/API/notebook language around most data platforms even when the heavy execution engine is native, JVM or distributed.
technologies.compatibility: For data work, verify wheels for NumPy/Pandas/PyArrow/Spark connectors before moving to a brand-new Python line.

technologies.name: Apache Spark / PySpark
highlights: Regular Python UDFs use Arrow optimization by default
Native GEOMETRY / GEOGRAPHY SQL types
Spark 4 distributions are built for Scala 2.13; Scala 2.12 support is dropped
technologies.whyItMatters: The Python/JVM boundary is getting cheaper, but built-in DataFrame/SQL expressions, shuffle design, pruning and file layout still matter more than language syntax at distributed scale.
technologies.compatibility: Spark 4.2.0 is the newest stable line in the official downloads; ecosystem connectors and table formats must be checked for Spark 4.2 compatibility.

technologies.name: Scala
technologies.productionBaseline: 3.9.0 LTS; 2.13.18 remains the current Scala 2 line
highlights: Scala 3.9 opens a new Long-Term Support line
The LTS/Next model separates conservative library baselines from faster feature delivery
technologies.whyItMatters: Scala remains useful for JVM-native Spark libraries and custom code, while PySpark/SQL increasingly cover most day-to-day data engineering.
technologies.compatibility: Scala 3.9 artifacts are not consumable by Scala 3.3 projects; Spark 4 prebuilt artifacts use Scala 2.13 rather than Scala 3.

technologies.name: Rust
technologies.nextPreview: beta/nightly channels continue on the six-week cadence
highlights: 1.98.1 is a point release fixing a vtable miscompilation from 1.98.0
Rust increasingly sits underneath modern analytical engines and infrastructure
technologies.whyItMatters: DuckDB-adjacent tooling, Polars, DataFusion and many new data systems use Rust to combine native performance with memory safety.
technologies.compatibility: Use rustup stable for production; pin the toolchain in CI for reproducible builds.

technologies.name: Java / JDK
technologies.nextPreview: JDK 28 follows the six-month release cadence
highlights: JDK 27 is the latest Java SE release
JDK 25 remains the current Long-Term Support release
technologies.whyItMatters: Spark, Kafka and much of the distributed-data ecosystem remain JVM-based even when users primarily write Python or SQL.
technologies.compatibility: Choose an LTS JDK when ecosystem support matters more than the newest language/runtime features; verify Spark/Kafka vendor matrices before jumping JDK versions.

technologies.name: DuckDB
highlights: DuckDB maintains a published release calendar
The project is approaching its 2.0 major release
technologies.whyItMatters: DuckDB is a strong single-node baseline for Parquet/SQL analytics and makes a useful control when deciding whether Spark/distributed compute is actually necessary.
technologies.compatibility: Pin extensions and client bindings with the engine version for reproducible benchmark results.

technologies.name: Polars
highlights: Polars 2.0 plans to make the streaming engine the default for LazyFrame queries
The 2.0 transition is primarily a defaults/API cleanup rather than a feature-reset release
technologies.whyItMatters: Polars is a fast single-node DataFrame alternative that can reduce the need for Spark on medium-sized local workloads.
technologies.compatibility: Treat Polars 2.0 as a migration event; benchmark memory/streaming behavior rather than assuming pandas-style semantics.

technologies.name: Apache Iceberg
highlights: 1.11.0 continues table-format evolution across engines
Java 11 and Spark 3.4 support are being deprecated/dropped in the 1.11 line
technologies.whyItMatters: Iceberg is central to multi-engine lakehouse interoperability, especially when storage/catalog ownership should not be tied to one compute vendor.
technologies.compatibility: Check the engine-specific Iceberg runtime artifact and catalog implementation, not only the table-format version.

technologies.name: Delta Lake
highlights: Delta Spark defaults to Spark 4.2
Catalog-managed tables and UC Delta APIs expand multi-engine/catalog-centric operation
Delta 4.4 continues Delta Kernel, UniForm and connector work
technologies.whyItMatters: Delta remains the native lakehouse table layer around Databricks/Spark while becoming more catalog-centric and interoperable.
technologies.compatibility: Delta 4.4 supports Spark 4.2 and continued 4.1/4.0.1 compatibility; verify exact engine/version matrix before upgrading.

technologies.name: Apache Airflow
highlights: Airflow 3.3.2 is the latest patch release in the 3.3 line
The project continues frequent 3.x patch/minor delivery
technologies.whyItMatters: Airflow remains a major general-purpose DAG orchestrator even as data platforms add more declarative and platform-native pipeline systems.
technologies.compatibility: Provider packages and executor/deployment choices should be versioned separately from core Airflow.

technologies.name: dbt OSS / Core
technologies.productionBaseline: 2.0.x; 1.12.5 remains available on the v1 line
highlights: dbt 2.0 is a ground-up Rust rewrite that underpins the Fusion engine
The new line broadens native adapter/materialization capabilities while the v1 Python line remains relevant for compatibility
technologies.whyItMatters: dbt demonstrates the same abstraction trend as SQL: users describe transformations/tests/contracts while the engine increasingly owns execution and optimization details.
technologies.compatibility: Treat the 1.x → 2.x move as a major migration; validate adapters, packages, macros and CI behavior before switching.
